attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 30 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. Its whole body is three sentences: he was a Studite monk and a disciple of Theodore the Studite, whose feast it gives parenthetically as 11 November, and after Theodore's death he took his teacher's place in the abbacy of the monastery; he was a fervent adherent of the veneration of the holy icons and died of hardships in exile as a confessor of the faith; and he was a Byzantine hymnographer of the ninth century, a poet of canons. **The display name is `Clement the Studite` and not `the Hymnographer`** because `hymnographer` is one of this folder's `types` and `lib/honorific.js` composes the rank itself; the page states both things. The `related` row is Theodore, the one man the page names and the one the corpus holds. It prints no hymn of his own and names no relic. The corpus's other Clements are of Rome, Ancyra, Ohrid, Sardis and Mount Sagmation.
